newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: RAINS DRAW LOCUST SWARMS FROM ZIMBABWE TO BOTSWANA.
newsitem.headline: RAINS DRAW LOCUST SWARMS FROM ZIMBABWE TO BOTSWANA.

text.p: Swarms of red locusts which have plagued Zimbabwe for the past three months have now flown away to neighbouring Botswana, drawn by recent rains, the Commercial Farmers' Union (CFU) said on Monday.
CFU spokesman Ben Zietsman said massive aerial sprays by the national agricultural, technical and extension services (Agritex) and the CFU had also killed many of the marauding flies last week.
"The recent rains in Botswana contributed to the westward mobility because they need moist, soft and damp soil for them to breed," Zietsman said in a statement.
The Zimbabwean army and police last week joined an intense fight by the CFU and Agritex to wipe out the locusts before the start of the new planting season this month.
The red locusts invaded Zimbabwe from neighbouring Mozambique in August, hitting mostly its southern and eastern districts.

The CFU said crop damage had so far been minimal, and confined mostly to winter irrigated crops, grass and leaves because the invasion came after the end of the 1995/96 (November-April) cropping season.
